title: Chapter 7 — Sugar
description: Whatever Sugar Palace becomes, it becomes today.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: NAPTIP holding cell. The girls who were on the bus give statements one by one. Each one says your name. Ivie does not visit.

beats.title: The Price of Italy
beats.summary: Half a million naira. That is what it cost. You will have years to count it.

beats.speaker: officerGrace
beats.text: (At the gate, with a certificate in a cheap frame.) Commendation. From the agency. (She looks at the bar.) I won't ask what you do here, Madam. I will ask what you will do next.

beats.speaker: blessing
beats.text: (Holding a hair dryer like a trophy.) Mama! The first customer at Blessing's Touch is you. Free. Forever.

variants.text: (Kemi, in her nursing school uniform for the first time.) Mama. Look. (She turns around once, like a model.)

beats.title: The Woman Who Said No
beats.summary: You were offered a million naira for five girls. You said no, and then you made sure nobody else could say yes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Three months later. SUGAR'S KITCHEN & SUITES. A real menu. Rooms by the night, with receipts. Kemi does the books. Precious runs the bar and makes everybody laugh. Ivie comes on weekends and argues with the cook.

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: Mummy, your pepper soup is the best in Lagos. Officially. (She shows you a food blogger's review. Four and a half stars. "Points off for the generator.")

beats.title: Sugar's Kitchen
beats.summary: You built it twice: once to survive, and once to be proud of. The second one has a menu.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Chief Dapo padlocked the hotel in the end. You did not fight him. You rented a stall at the market instead, a pot of pepper soup and four plastic chairs.

beats.speaker: ivie
beats.text: (Serving a customer, school bag still on her back.) Two bowls, one Coke! Mummy, we are running out of goat!

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Kemi comes on Sundays in a white uniform, eats two bowls, and complains about night shifts like a woman who is very happy.

beats.title: Mama, Just Mama
beats.summary: Smaller. Poorer. Lighter. Your daughter calls you to her school's PTA meetings now. You go.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: GOLDEN FLEECE II. You are very good at your job. Rukky gives you a bonus at Christmas and a Hilux at Easter. You sleep at night. That is the strange part.

beats.title: Golden Fleece II
beats.summary: You sold your name to keep your house. The house is very nice. The name was yours.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Sugar Palace becomes the biggest hotel on South Street. Golden Fleece closes. Bassey eats your pepper soup every Friday and calls you "Madam" without laughing.

beats.speaker: kokoro
beats.text: (Awake, for once.) Mama, you are the queen of South Street now. (He doesn't say it like a compliment. He says it like weather.)

beats.title: Queen of South Street
beats.summary: You made it. Everybody on South Street knows your name, and nobody says it out loud.
